promises.promise: Triggers: what starts work without anyone asking. A trigger fires in code and drops an item in someone's inbox. A non-empty inbox is what starts an agent or notifies a person.
Lists what is standing and what is due.
Fires on a time, a pull request changing, an answer arriving or a job stopping.
Drops an item in an inbox, or runs an operation that needs no agent.
Holds an agent's triggers while the agent is paused.
Who set it: the household, an agent or a person.
A pull request changing can fire a trigger.
Waiting on an approval is a once-only trigger on that answer.
A job stopping can fire a trigger.
A trigger never wakes anyone directly. It drops an item in an inbox, with trigger as its source.
The agent's body starts in that conversation and takes everything waiting at once.

A schedule is a standing time trigger. A lane is a standing time trigger with instructions. A one-off wake is a time trigger that fires once. Waiting on an approval is a once-only trigger on that answer.

A trigger fires in code, with no model. It drops an item in the recipient's inbox. After a short settle time, a non-empty inbox starts an agent's body or notifies a person, with everything waiting at once. Pausing an agent holds its triggers.
Each part contributes a short list of what is open and how long it has sat. One session per recipient sorts them. When nothing is open, no session starts.

Each recipient sets a volume on an inbox item. Dim returns to full when the item changes or has sat long enough. Mute ends after a week by default. A change breaks dim but not mute. Being asked by name breaks both.
The timings are settings a person can change, each with a default. Loom keeps a row only for a person or agent that has changed them.
a What it carries. A trigger names who set it, the agent or person it is for, and its project.
b Who sees it. A household owner sees everything, including what is private to another member. Anyone else sees triggers in their projects and triggers for agents they own.
c Checked at the door. Loom applies this to callers from outside: a person, an agent, a machine, someone's own program. Loom's own parts read without asking.
The trigger detail shows its source, lifespan, target and words.
The trigger offers Run now, Cancel and Pause agent.
An answer arriving while the agent is paused does not fire its trigger.
Resuming fires the held once-only answer trigger exactly once.
Run now delivers one person Inbox item, then the whole waiting batch notifies after settling.
Cancelling a future trigger prevents delivery beyond its deadline.
